conversation.Statement: Hello, this is Nathan Carter from the IRS Tax Relief Department. I'm calling to let you know you qualify for a special refund on your 2023 taxes.
Oh, really? I wasn't expecting anything. Are you sure this is about my taxes?

Yes, ma'am. Our records indicate you overpaid on your federal taxes last year, and the IRS is issuing refunds to eligible citizens like yourself. I just need to verify some details to get your $3,100 refund processed.
Three thousand one hundred dollars? That would really help. What do you need me to do?
First, I need to confirm your identity for tax security reasons. Can you please provide your full name and the last four digits of your Social Security number?
My name is Martha Leonard, and the last four are 2684.

Thank you, Martha. Everything matches our records. Now, because of increased IRS security protocols, there is a one-time identity clearance fee of $247. This ensures your refund isn't delayed or intercepted.
A fee? But I thought refunds were just sent out automatically. I live on Social Security, I can't afford extra charges.

I understand completely. Unfortunately, these IRS security measures are mandatory for all refunds over $2,000. If we don't get this processed today, your refund application will be suspended, and you may not receive any disbursement.
Suspended? Will that affect my Social Security or Medicare?

If the refund is flagged and not cleared, it can trigger an IRS review of your benefits. We don't want that to happen. It's very important to resolve this now to prevent any issues with your government payments.
That sounds scary. What do I have to do to pay this fee?
The IRS accepts clearance fees via secure methods only. You can either purchase three $100 Apple gift cards or use Zelle to transfer the funds directly. Which would be easier for you?
I think I can get gift cards at the pharmacy near me. Do I just buy them and call you back?
Actually, please stay on the line while you purchase them. It's important we don't disconnect, so I can guide you and make sure the payment is properly registered with the IRS system.
Alright, I'll get ready and go now. Can you just remind me what kind of card to get again?
Three Apple gift cards, each for $100. Once you have them, scratch off the codes and read them to me. We'll process it immediately so your refund isn't delayed.
Okay, but this is definitely going to the IRS, right? I don't want to mess up my benefits.

Absolutely, Martha. I work directly with the IRS Tax Relief Department. This is standard procedure, if you don't complete the payment today, your refund and potentially your benefits could be frozen until next tax season.
I really can't wait that long. I'll go to the store now. Please hold on.
